newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares edge down from record high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares edge down from record high.

text.p: The Jakarta share index edged lower on profit-taking mainly in blue chips on Friday after touching a new high of 710.43 points in early trading.
The index closed down 2.89 points, or 0.41 percent, at 704.48 points. It rose 10.2 points during the three trading days this week after closing at 694.28 on February 6.
Decliners leading advancers by 64 to 50, with 61 counters unchanged on Friday. Turnover was about 613 billion rupiah on a volume of 246.3 million shares.
Brokers expected prices to rebound again on Monday with the return of many domestic players following the Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr holidays.
"Many players will re-enter the bourse next week after their extended holiday," a foreign broker said. "It should help boost market activity."

Brokers and analysts said banking stocks were likely to continue to attract attention on expectations that the sector would post better 1997 earnings with a further possible cut in interest rates and on market talk of possible bank mergers.
Expectations of higher 1996 earnings results in some counters were also likely to boost overall market sentiment, brokers said.
Blue-chip Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list with 31.6 million shares traded, falling 50 rupiah to 1,725 rupiah on profit-taking, brokers said.
State-controlled tin miner Tambang Timah was active and made gains on market speculation that it might become involved in the Busang gold find in East Kalimantan, brokers said.
It rose 7.11 percent to close at 5,275 rupiah on 11.7 million shares.
Secondary salt producer Fiskaragung closed 500 rupiah higher at 4,350 rupiah with about four million shares traded.
Brokers said the rise followed a company statement that its unaudited 1996 net profit result of 82 billion rupiah was higher than its IPO target of 71.8 billion rupiah.

Fiskaragung's sister company Davomas, which engages in cocoa processing, was also actively traded on expectations of better-than-expected 1996 earnings. Davomas rose 13.71 percent to 3,525 rupiah on 2.6 million shares.
Integrated poultry and fast food firm Sierad Produce was also active on foreign-buying, brokers said. It rose 25 rupiah to 900 rupiah on 4.3 million shares.

Sierad Produce's assistant to president director Awi Tantra said Malaysia's integrated poultry and fast food chain KFC Holdings (Malaysia) Bhd had bought 50 million shares of PT Sierad Produce from the bourse.
This represents a 6.78 percent stake in the Indonesian firm.
